takeaway: One more humid, showery day, then the pattern turns. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has Nicoya near 34°C today with isolated afternoon storms and coastal showers around the peninsula tonight. From Wednesday the Caribbean trades push back in, and the models now spread that breeze over the Nicoya Peninsula from Thursday into early next week, with rain shifting to the Caribbean side. For surf, today's wind is southeast to south (side-on to onshore), so it's a so-so day. Offshore northeast winds return Wednesday, with a firmer push Thursday. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch drops a notch.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Tue–Thu, Oct 20–22)
periods.pattern: IMN's Tuesday forecast for the North Pacific calls for a partly cloudy morning, then partly to mostly cloudy skies with isolated downpours and thunder in the afternoon. Tonight it expects coastal showers around the Nicoya Peninsula. Nicoya's high is about 34°C and the low about 24°C. IMN says the band of tropical showers is still close to the country and the air over both seas is very moist. Its weekly outlook says Monday to Wednesday are the most important rain days this week. The model averages put roughly 10–20 mm (about 0.4–0.75 inch) near Nosara in the 24 hours ending this evening, with heavier rain just offshore. Wednesday looks lighter, around 8–10 mm (about a third of an inch). Thursday drops to a few millimeters as the trades take over.
periods.implications: Mornings are the best outdoor window today and Wednesday. Expect a chance of an afternoon storm and showers near the coast tonight. Thursday should feel noticeably drier and breezier.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on the showery start and the turn to trades by Thursday. Moderate on exactly where today's storms hit.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Fri–Mon, Oct 23–26)
periods.pattern: All three ensemble averages now spread the northeast-to-east trades across northern Costa Rica and the Nicoya Peninsula from Thursday through Monday. Rain shifts to the Caribbean slopes, which is the classic dry-season-style setup. Near Nosara the averages show only light daily amounts, mostly a few millimeters. The main European run is the outlier, with a wetter blip near the peninsula Friday into Saturday. IMN's weekly outlook expects the first cold push of the season to reach the northern Caribbean this weekend. It won't affect Costa Rica much directly, but it should bring drier air and occasional moderate winds to the North Pacific.
periods.implications: A good stretch for outdoor plans: sunnier, drier, and breezy. Keep a light rain layer handy Friday or Saturday in case the wetter European run is right.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on the breezier, drier trend. Moderate on whether a stray shower day sneaks in Friday or Saturday.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Tue Oct 27 – Tue Nov 3)
periods.pattern: The ensembles keep easterly trades across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica into early November, with mostly light rain near Nosara and the wetter areas over the Caribbean side and far offshore to the south. IMN expects very dry conditions on the North Pacific from Oct 26 through Nov 8, with below-normal rain and low odds of an extreme event (about 10% for Oct 25–Nov 1). The hurricane center's system near southern Mexico stays far to our northwest.
periods.implications: Good odds that the dry season starts to show up: mostly sunny, breezy days and cooler nights to close out October.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on the drier trend matching IMN. Low on day-to-day details.

surfWinds.regime: Pacific side-on/onshore today, then Caribbean trades (offshore at Nosara) from Wednesday, getting firmer Thursday and holding into the weekend. This is the most solid offshore setup in about a week.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 1:48 a.m. PDT Tuesday, 2:48 a.m. Costa Rica time) has southeast to south winds at 10–15 knots today, which is side-on to onshore at Nosara, and south winds tonight turning west to northwest late. Wednesday flips to northeast to east 15–20 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo and north to northeast around 10 knots elsewhere, which is offshore here. Wednesday night is northeast to east 15–20 in the gulf and northeast 10–15 elsewhere. Thursday is northeast 15–20 knots. Friday and Saturday ease to northeast to east around 10 knots. The forecasters say the Papagayo winds will pulse each night, with strong pulses possible late this week. Swell: south to southwest 5–7 feet at 14 seconds today and Wednesday. A longer-period pulse shows up Wednesday night (4–6 feet at 17 seconds), then 5–7 feet at 15 seconds Thursday, easing to 4–6 feet Friday and Saturday and 3–5 feet by Saturday night. Nicaragua: every ensemble keeps easterly trades over Nicaragua the whole two weeks, strengthening into the weekend, so Nicaragua should be offshore all day on most days. That's a strong sign of good wind quality for Nosara mornings. Unlike yesterday, the models also spread the trades over Nicoya Thursday through Monday, so offshore may hold later into the day on the windier days. Still, don't count on all-day offshore here every day; afternoon sea breezes can still sneak in. Lightning: storms are possible this afternoon, so get out of the water if you hear thunder.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today: early morning is your best bet before the southerly breeze fills in, but expect some texture. Wednesday morning: offshore returns with solid 14-second south-southwest swell. Thursday morning: probably the pick of the week, with firmer northeast trades and the swell back up to 15 seconds after the long-period pulse arrives overnight. Friday to Sunday mornings: clean offshore wind likely, with the swell slowly getting smaller.
surfWinds.confidence: High on side-on/onshore today and offshore returning Wednesday from the marine forecast. Moderate-high on firm trades Thursday through the weekend. Moderate on how late into each day the offshore holds.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, nothing established, and down a notch. The models now bring the trades back over Nicoya instead of a lingering Pacific flow.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: If anything, today and Wednesday (Oct 20–21) while the shower band stays close. Risk drops from Thursday.
gyreWatch.supporting: IMN keeps the tropical shower band near Costa Rica today with very moist air over both seas, and expects coastal showers around Nicoya tonight. The model averages still show about 10–20 mm near Nosara in the 24 hours ending this evening, with heavier rain offshore. The main European run has a wetter blip near the peninsula Friday into Saturday.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model shows a broad, slow-spinning low near Costa Rica. All the ensembles bring northeast-to-east trades over Nicaragua and Nicoya from Thursday through early next week, which is the opposite of a prolonged-soak setup (that needs a steady Pacific wind for days). IMN's weekly outlook calls for drying by the weekend with the first cold push in the northern Caribbean, and its long-range outlook calls for below-normal rain through Nov 8 with low odds of an extreme event. The hurricane center's system south of Mexico stays far to the northwest and moves away. Nothing is expected in the Caribbean. The U.S. tropics discussion (Oct 13) says trades are strengthening north of the equator and doesn't mention a Central American gyre.

whatChanged: The marine forecast now has today's wind southeast to south all day (side-on to onshore), instead of an east morning turning onshore in the afternoon. The offshore return moved a bit earlier, to Wednesday daytime, and the forecasters added possible strong Papagayo pulses late this week. The bigger change is in the models. Yesterday several kept a soft Pacific flow over Nosara mid to late week. Today all three ensembles spread the trades over Nicoya from Thursday into early next week and move the rain to the Caribbean side. IMN's new weekly outlook calls for the first cold push in the northern Caribbean this weekend, bringing drier air and occasional moderate winds to the North Pacific. Tropical Storm Trudy is no longer on the hurricane center's map, and the new system south of Mexico is still at 90% and moving away from us. The prolonged-rain watch is down a notch.
practical: Today: get outdoor things done in the morning, expect heat around 34°C, and plan for a possible afternoon storm and showers near the coast tonight. Surf early, but expect a side-on texture. Wednesday: offshore wind is back, so a morning session looks good; a few showers are still possible later. Thursday: likely the best surf morning of the week, and the start of a drier, breezier stretch. Friday through the weekend: good for beach days and outdoor plans; bring a light layer in case of a stray shower Friday or Saturday. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
